habitat: Singly or in pairs in virtually any open grassland, including urban areas.
summary: A common resident, the most widespread pipit in Newman’s account. Light brown, with bold facial markings, a boldly marked breast, white outer tail feathers and a yellow base to the bill. The disturbance call is chissik, with a dipping flight. The male’s display is chree-chree-chree-chree during each dip. The Kemp paper name Grassveld Pipit and the code RB were left unchanged.

tail.shape: White outer tail feathers, not buff.

calls.description: A diagnostic chissik when disturbed. The male also gives chree-chree-chree-chree during each dip of the display flight. Grade A call and flight call from Wildealskloof, Bloemfontein. The filename is XC938658-OSF1561_92_PipitAfrican_WildealskloofBFN_0241006.mp3.

similar.note: Plain-backed Pipit is faintly streaked grey-brown above, with a strong white eyebrow and only light breast streaking. African Pipit has a boldly marked breast and white outer tail feathers.
